newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan deals stiff penalties to scandal-hit firms.
newsitem.headline: Japan deals stiff penalties to scandal-hit firms.

text.p: Japan on Wednesday imposed stiff penalties on two top financial institutions implicated in a widening racketeer payoff scandal, Nomura Securities Co Ltd and Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank (DKB).

The Ministry of Finance (MOF) ordered the suspension of key parts of Nomura and DKB's businesses for various durations, some as long as a year. Both firms were also barred from underwriting government bonds until the end of this year.
DKB and Nomura are both entangled in a high-profile scandal involving payoffs to a "sokaiya" corporate racketeer.

More than a dozen people, including top executives from the two financial firms, have been arrested in the affair, which coincides with the start of "Big Bang" reforms aimed at introducing more competition and global standards into Japan's long-sheltered financial sector.

On Wednesday morning, prosecutors raided the headquarters of Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd, one of Japan's "Big Four" brokers along with Nomura, to search for evidence of illegal payoffs amid signs that the affair could widen still further.
Payoffs to sokaiya, who extort money by threatening to disrupt shareholders meetings or by offering to prevent others doing so, are illegal.
